rit_meaning: Size of the PDF file in kilobytes.
rationale: Same broad size concept, but the official CIC page does not state its unit and the mirror must not be assumed byte-identical or identically scaled.

rit_meaning: Size of metadata extracted from the PDF file, in bytes.
rationale: Both dictionaries describe metadata-section size; compatible numeric quantity, with CIC's observed -1 raw sentinel retained and separately audited.

rit_meaning: Number of pages in the PDF file.
rationale: Same page-count concept, but RIT documents corrupted files as pages=0 while CIC has observed -1 values with no verified CIC sentinel semantics.

rit_meaning: xref length as extracted from the file header.
rationale: Both dictionaries describe the Xref length/entry quantity; local maxima and numeric representation are compatible evidence, while CIC -1 remains an unverified raw sentinel.

rit_meaning: Number of characters in the file title.
rationale: Both dictionaries describe the number of title characters; compatible numeric character count, with CIC's raw -1 sentinel retained.

rit_meaning: 1 if the file is encrypted; 0 otherwise.
rationale: Related encryption indicator, but CIC observed values extend beyond binary 0/1 and its special-value representation is unverified.

rit_meaning: Number of embedded files inside the PDF, as extracted from the header.
rationale: Both dictionaries describe a count of embedded files and use a numeric local representation; no unit conversion is required.

rit_meaning: Number of images in the PDF file.
rationale: Same image-count concept, but CIC stores category strings and includes malformed lexical values such as 1(1); no coercion is defensible yet.

rit_meaning: Whether the file contains at least the default threshold of 50 text characters.
rationale: RIT is a documented >=50-character ternary signal; CIC documents text presence with Yes/No/unclear/-1/0 values. These are not established as equivalent.

rit_meaning: PDF version extracted from the file header.
rationale: CIC documents valid-header presence, whereas RIT stores a numeric extracted PDF version. Header strings must not be treated as a version transform without verification.

rit_meaning: Number of occurrences of the string "obj" in the PDF file.
rationale: RIT counts obj string occurrences; CIC documents indirect objects and also has malformed category values. Parser/count equivalence is not established.

rit_meaning: Number of occurrences of the string "endobj" in the PDF file.
rationale: Related name, but the CIC official page does not separately define Endobj and raw values include non-numeric text.

rit_meaning: Number of occurrences of the string "stream" in the PDF file.
rationale: RIT counts stream string occurrences; CIC documents streams as binary-data sequences. Equal parser/count semantics are not established.

rit_meaning: Number of occurrences of the string "endstream" in the PDF file.
rationale: Related name, but CIC Endstream is not separately defined in the official feature descriptions and raw values are malformed in places.

rit_meaning: Number of occurrences of the string "trailer" in the PDF file.
rationale: Both dictionaries describe a count of PDF trailers and use numeric local representations.

rit_meaning: Number of occurrences of the string "xref" in the PDF file.
rationale: RIT counts xref occurrences while CIC documents Xref tables; count semantics are related but not proven equal.

rit_meaning: Number of occurrences of the string "startxref" in the PDF file.
rationale: Related startxref keyword count, but CIC includes malformed raw strings and exact parser behavior is not documented.

rit_meaning: Number of occurrences of the string "/Page" in the PDF file.
rationale: Both appear page-related, but CIC PageNo is not separately defined and is not proven to count the /Page keyword.

rit_meaning: Number of occurrences of the string "/Encrypt" in the PDF file.
rationale: Related names, but CIC's Encrypt column is distinct from isEncrypted and is not separately defined on the official page.

rit_meaning: Number of occurrences of the string "/ObJStm" in the PDF file.
rationale: Both dictionaries describe stream objects (ObjStm) as a numeric count.

rit_meaning: Number of occurrences of the string "/JS" in the PDF file.
rationale: Both refer to JS-related keywords/objects, but CIC's category values contain unverified malformed encodings such as 1(1).

rit_meaning: Number of occurrences of the string "/JavaScript" in the PDF file.
